title: Winterspring
body: Winterspring is a high valley of snow and ice in the mountains of northern Kalimdor, east of Felwood, north of Azshara and northeast of Mount Hyjal. Most travelers reach it through the tunnels of Timbermaw Hold. Long ago the night elves raised the city of Kel'Theril here, and beside its ruins the cursed spirits of Highborne still drift over a frozen lake. In the Third War Tyrande Whisperwind and Malfurion Stormrage fought across these snows and woke the Druids of the Talon from their barrow dens. Today the goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel keep the trading post of Everlook at the crossroads of the valley, and night elves hold Starfall Village to its northwest. Frostsabers prowl the northern heights, maddened wildkin guard old sacred places, and the Winterfall furbolgs have turned savage. Blue dragons lair in the caverns of Mazthoril, frost giants hold a canyon in the south, and beyond it, in Darkwhisper Gorge, demons stand between the valley and the heights of Hyjal.

title: Frostfire Hot Springs
body: At the far western end of Winterspring, close to the mouth of Timbermaw Hold, steaming pools break through the snow. No volcano lies anywhere near them, and that riddle has drawn the dwarf Donova Snowden, who keeps watch beside one of the springs and has found that their water has strange qualities. She suspects something far more threatening than fire beneath the earth, and believes its source lies at the southern end of the valley, where the air turns thick and muggy and the sky grows dark. The Winterfall furbolgs are drawn to the springs as well. Their pathfinders and den watchers guard the two larger pools fiercely and drive off anyone who comes near.

title: Timbermaw Post
body: Southeast of the road that runs from the hot springs toward the heart of Winterspring lies Timbermaw Post, a small furbolg camp. Its name suggests that the Timbermaw of the nearby hold once kept it, but the camp now belongs wholly to the Winterfall tribe, whose den watchers and pathfinders stand guard there while owlbeasts and shardtooth bears roam the slopes around it. Salfa, who guards the Winterspring gate of the hold, remembers that the Winterfall were once allies of the Timbermaw, until the strange demands of a high chief turned them against everyone they met.

title: Lake Kel'Theril
body: In the center of Winterspring lies Lake Kel'Theril, frozen hard beneath the mountain wind. Long ago Highborne sorcerers stole a sacred relic, hoping to siphon its power and become greater still. Their ritual failed. The relic shattered in a tremendous explosion, and its pieces were driven deep beneath the ice of the lake. The thieves were cursed to remain where they had worked their folly, and their suffering, anguished spirits still drift over the frozen water, searching for fragments of the very thing that doomed them. Chimaerae, bears and owlbeasts hunt along the shore.

title: The Ruins of Kel'Theril
body: On the shore of Lake Kel'Theril lie the remains of a great Highborne city, broken in the Great Sundering ten thousand years ago. Among its fallen stones walk the spirits of the Highborne who died here, suffering and anguished, still bound by the curse of the relic their people stole. Nearly all of them are lost in their own misery and cannot be reached. One alone, a remorseful spirit, speaks of its sorrow and of a past that cannot be undone. The night elf Ranshalla has studied the carvings on these stones and believes they hold the incantations of an ancient altar of Elune.

title: Starfall Village
body: Starfall Village is a small night elf settlement on the main road between Everlook and Frostsaber Rock, and the only Alliance outpost in Winterspring. A lodge and a smaller house shelter sellers of food, goods and trade supplies, and the village keeps the old Ban'Thallow Barrow Den. Wynd Nightchaser spends most of his days here and knows a great deal about the valley and its secrets. A dwarf has come as well, Jaron Stoneshaper of the Explorers' League, who hunts the magical artifacts said to lie in Winterspring, most of them fiercely guarded. He rests here now, after the wildkin chased him from his camp.

title: Frostsaber Rock
body: In the far north of Winterspring a great tor juts above the snow, and around it gather the frostsabers, the most feral and hardest to tame of all the great cats. Their matriarch is Shy-Rotam, whose stone stands among the pride. About four thousand years ago Tyrande Whisperwind saved the frostsaber queen from rampaging giants, and since that day the cats have been allies of the night elves. Huntresses, stalkers and pride watchers roam among the cubs, and a great cat called Rak'shiri hunts among them. At the top of the rock the night elf Rivern Frostwind and his companion Glacier patiently train frostsabers to carry riders.

title: Everlook
body: Everlook is a trading post of the Steamwheedle Cartel, built where the main trade routes of Winterspring meet. Like the Cartel's other towns it is neutral ground, and its goblin bruisers have no patience for anyone who spills blood within its walls. An inn, a market and the only bank in the valley serve travelers of every race. The town draws curious company: Gregor Greystone speaks for the Argent Dawn before the local governance, Malyfous Darkhammer represents the Thorium Brotherhood, a troll witch doctor makes lucky charms, and a stern tauren sets trials for the bold.

title: Mazthoril
body: Mazthoril is a deep cavern of ice in central Winterspring, near Lake Kel'Theril and Everlook, and the home of the blue dragonflight in these lands. Cobalt wyrmkin, scalebanes and mageweavers guard its frozen halls among whelps, broodlings and spell eaters, while the drakes Spellmaw, Manaclaw and Scryer keep watch and the blue General Colbatann stalks its passages. At the heart of it all dwells Haleh, the matron protectorate of the flight. Her chamber at the cavern's peak is reached only by magic: cobalt runes set into the icy floor carry those who hold one of the flight's scales up to her.

title: Ice Thistle Hills
body: Southeast of Everlook rise the Ice Thistle Hills, the country of the Ice Thistle yeti. They make their home in a cave high in the hills and roam the snowy slopes around it, and their great patriarchs and matriarchs carry the largest horns of their kind. Chillwind chimaerae and shardtooth bears hunt the same ground. The yeti know little peace, for their thick fur and pristine horns are prized in Everlook, where Umi Rumplesnicker wants both for a mechanical yeti of her own. A blue dragon named Azurous roams the hills as well.

title: Winterfall Village
body: Far to the east lies Winterfall Village, the home of the Winterfall furbolgs. The tribe was never known for aggression, yet its ursa, shamans and den watchers now fall upon nearly anything that comes near. The Timbermaw say the change began with the strange demands of High Chief Winterfall, who keeps to the mouth of a cave at the edge of the village. His people carry flasks that hold a strange green liquid, one that almost glows. The fierce Grizzle Snowpaw prowls the camp, and yeti and shardtooth bears roam nearby.

title: The Hidden Grove
body: In the northeast of Winterspring a forested crater lies hidden behind high cliffs on every side. The only ordinary way in is a cave in the southeastern face of the ridge, though a bold climber might risk the drop from the cliffs above. Within lies a haunt of moontouched owlbeasts, the hostile wildkin of the northern valley, which are fiercer than their kin elsewhere in Winterspring. A few crazed and berserk owlbeasts live among them, and more of their moontouched kind roam the snowy ground beyond the cliffs.

title: Owl Wing Thicket
body: Owl Wing Thicket is a series of caves along a ridge in southern Winterspring, overrun by crazed, berserk and moontouched owlbeasts. Horde runners report that these wildkin seem to have gone mad from exposure to the very thing they guard. At the foot of the ridge waits the night elf Ranshalla, a colleague of the scholar Erelas Ambersky, fresh from studying the Ruins of Kel'Theril and determined to learn why the wildkin defend this place so fiercely. At the top of the ridge lies what she believes to be an ancient altar of the goddess Elune, which she hopes to open by lighting the torches in the caves while old incantations are spoken over it.

title: Dun Mandarr
body: Dun Mandarr is a small camp beside an icy cavern in southeastern Winterspring, set up by the dwarf Jaron Stoneshaper of the Explorers' League. It did not last. Soon after Jaron unearthed an amulet at his dig site, bloodthirsty wildkin fell upon the camp, smashing his crates and wagon and chasing him away, and he fears a friend of his was not so lucky. Owlbeasts and screeching owls now haunt the wreckage, and what remains of his tools lies half buried in the snow. One crate has been smashed open, almost as if it were exactly what the beasts were after.

title: Frostwhisper Gorge
body: Frostwhisper Gorge is a deep canyon in the south of Winterspring, held by the frostmaul giants, great beings of solid ice. Shards of ice litter its floor, reflective enough to catch the light like mirrors and prized by those who make charms. These are the same giants from whom Tyrande Whisperwind once saved the frostsaber queen, and Rivern Frostwind still asks friends of the frostsabers to strike them down in Shy-Rotam's name. A brute called Kashoch the Reaver walks among them. Night elf ruins lie along the ridges, where a satyr named Lorax paces in an old temple, and a great bridge spans the chasm toward Darkwhisper Gorge.

title: Darkwhisper Gorge
body: In the far south of Winterspring the air turns thick and muggy and the sky grows dark. This is Darkwhisper Gorge, a maze of tunnels and chasms where demons have made their home, led by Lady Hederine and her manastalkers, slayers and initiates. The demons are not the gorge's only odd residents. An imp named Vi'el keeps a shop of exotic reagents in a cave, and seems startled when a customer slips past the minion at his door, and at the bottom of the gorge the high elf Earthcaller Franzahl studies the elements. Deeper still, a runed gateway faces toward Mount Hyjal, sealed and silent.

title: Donova Snowden
body: Donova Snowden is a dwarf who came to Winterspring to study the Frostfire Hot Springs and has camped beside them a long while since. Cold, vast and dismal as the valley may seem, she calls it a place of many secrets. Her friend Krakle of Un'Goro sends curious travelers her way, for these springs steam with no volcano anywhere near, and Meggi Peppinrocker of Everlook sends those who would help with trouble. Donova has found that the water has strange qualities, and she suspects a far more threatening cause than any fire beneath the earth. The Winterfall furbolgs who guard the larger springs make her studies hard.

body: Haleh is the matron protectorate of the blue dragonflight, a consort of Malygos who dwells at the peak of Mazthoril and receives visitors in the guise of a high elf. The Aspects insist that dragons stay out of mortal affairs, yet Haleh will not stand idle while one of their own kind scorns that law. Nefarian, of the cursed brood of Deathwing, schemes behind the protection of Blackrock Mountain toward ends the blue flight cannot allow. Because the mountain makes it ever harder for the flight to intercede, Haleh offers her power to mortals instead, warning that the path before them is full of peril and the choice theirs to ponder.

body: Rivern Frostwind is a night elf who lives atop Frostsaber Rock with his companion Glacier, training the wild frostsabers of Winterspring to bear riders. He calls them the most feral and difficult to subdue of all the sabers, and he will sell one only to the most trusted, who must earn acceptance from him and from the cats alike. Those who would prove themselves begin humbly, gathering meat to feed the sabers in training, then drive the crazed Winterfall furbolgs from the rock and strike at the frostmaul giants in the name of Shy-Rotam. Discipline and determination, he says, are what he asks above all.

title: Witch Doctor Mau'ari
body: Witch Doctor Mau'ari is a jungle troll who has made a home among the goblins of Everlook and claims she always knows what a visitor has come for. From the reflective shards of the frostmaul giants she makes a lucky charm, the Cache of Mau'ari. Carried on the hunt, it lets its bearer capture e'ko, the spiritual power every creature holds, from the frostsabers, wildkin, yeti and other beasts of the valley. Mau'ari knows an incantation that turns e'ko into juju, and the charm's shining surface reflects that power onto whoever holds it: the speed of the frostsaber, or the keen mind of the wildkin.

All who have gone up against Ursius, Storm warns, have quickly found themselves the prey and Ursius the hunter, so a challenger must stay on guard and strike before the bear discovers their intent.

title: Earthcaller Franzahl
body: At the bottom of Darkwhisper Gorge, among the demons, waits Earthcaller Franzahl, a high elf who studies the known and unknown elements of the world. No mortal has spoken the word elementium to him in decades. His former student Krixix, a goblin, spent a lifetime trying to reach the chained gods of the underworld and what would form only where the elements clash. Nearly a decade ago Krixix opened a fissure in this very gorge, and an agent of Therazane sprang out of it. The two spoke, then the fissure closed and Krixix was gone, swallowed whole. Franzahl warns that what one wishes for may become what one does not want.

title: Lorax
body: Lorax is a satyr who paces the ruins of a night elf temple above Frostwhisper Gorge, talking to himself. Mock him as mad and he threatens to rip out your tongue; ask what he does and he answers that he broods, laments, hates and plots, then broods again. He dreams of catching Goraluk Anvilcrack. Lorax agreed to teach that Blackrock orc the secret of demon forging in exchange for his soul, a poor price, though in such times any soul is better than none. Goraluk ran off with the unforged, rune-covered breastplate without paying, and Lorax suspects he cowers in Blackrock Spire, trying to finish it without the knowledge only Lorax holds.

Few stop to wonder what a lone and friendly tauren is doing so far out in the frozen wilds, or why he seems so eager for company.

Salfa tells them that the Winterfall of this frozen land were once allies of the Timbermaw, until the strange demands of their high chief turned them on everything they met. parts.body: Trust among so wary a tribe must be earned again and again. The Winterfall carry spirit beads to ward off foul spirits, charms that have plainly failed, since the Winterfall themselves have become agents of corruption, and every set brought to Salfa is spoken of among the Timbermaw.
sources: quest 8469 request text and reward text

parts.body: A ritual totem taken from the Winterfall, heavy with dread and despair, reaches Kernda inside the hold. It has the shape of a Winterfall totem, yet it has been twisted by forces she cannot begin to comprehend, and whatever taint set the Winterfall against her tribe is surely in it. The Timbermaw will study it, hoping that one day the Winterfall will rage against them no more.
sources: quest 8471 description and reward text

title: The Crystal of Zin-Malor
body: Ivy Leafrunner in Felwood and Daryn Lightwind of Rut'theran Village send the curious to Winterspring, a harsh land full of ancient elven ruins, and to Wynd Nightchaser of Starfall Village, who knows the area well. Wynd tells the tale of Kel'Theril, a cursed race bound to the place of an unfortunate ritual. Highborne there once stole a sacred relic, believing they could siphon its power for themselves, but it shattered in a great explosion and its pieces were driven beneath the ice of the lake. For more, Wynd sends visitors to the dwarf Jaron Stoneshaper, who has lately seen the place himself.

parts.body: Jaron is no historian, but he has seen the spirits of Kel'Theril, miserable creatures still searching for pieces of the relic that cursed them. He lends his pick to dig the fragments out of the ice, and though he cannot say what they are, he knows someone who might: Aurora Skycaller, who lives near the Northpass Tower in the Eastern Plaguelands.
sources: quest 5244 reward text
quest 5245 description

parts.body: Aurora would rather not speak of the high elves' past, for it pains her that there is no way to make things right. Yet she names the shards: the Crystal of Zin-Malor, which can contain and control strong arcane forces and might have served good ends, had the evil intent of its thieves not shattered it. To mend it she needs sacred writings from the Temple of Zin-Malor in Azshara.
sources: quest 5245 reward text
quest 5246 description

parts.body: With the writings, an enchanted thorium bar, crystal restoratives and water from the dire pool of Dire Maul, Aurora fuses the fragments whole. She weeps that the elves too have been shattered as a race, and asks that the crystal be carried back to Lake Kel'Theril and shown to a spirit who understands the error of what was done long ago.
sources: quest 5247 description and reward text
quest 5248 description

parts.body: Most of the spirits are lost in their misery, but one remorseful soul knows the error of the past. At the sight of the crystal it calls out to its brethren that the Crystal of Zin-Malor is whole once again, and that they may let go of the past and rest. The crystal, it insists, must be returned.
sources: creature_text 10684 (said by smart_scripts 10684 on the 5248 turn-in)
quest 5252 description

parts.body: Wynd can hardly believe it. The crystal can never go back to its temple, which lies in ruin, and only a handful of the strongest magic users could ever control its power, so he sends it to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus, to be kept by those who will not abuse it.
sources: quest 5252 reward text
quest 5253 description

parts.body: Fandral has heard of the Crystal of Zin-Malor: its user gains incredible arcane power, but only if truly worthy. He is impressed that its bearer knew their own limits and never tried to wield it. The druids will keep it safe, and he hopes the cursed spirits that once guarded the shattered crystal may finally be at peace.
sources: quest 5253 reward text

title: The Altar of Elune
body: Erelas Ambersky of Rut'theran Village has found that wildkin feathers from the Hinterlands carry traces of magic, not wielded by the creatures but inherent in them, part of their very essence. He has heard that a large population of wildkin lives in the snows of Winterspring, and he wonders whether they share the same power. So he asks for moontouched feathers fallen to the ground in that valley, hoping to learn where such powers could have come from. He believes he is on the right track.

parts.body: The Winterspring feathers hold the same enchantment. Erelas, still unsure what may be found, sends their gatherer after a colleague of his, Ranshalla, who has gone into eastern Winterspring to watch the wildkin in their own home.
sources: quest 979 description

parts.body: Ranshalla waits below Owl Wing Thicket, fresh from the Ruins of Kel'Theril, where she copied incantations carved in the stone. She believes an altar of Elune lies at the top of the ridge, and that lighting the torches in each cave while she recites the spell will open it. She sets out up through the owlbeast caves with company at her side.

parts.body: Torch by torch, the altar at the summit begins to glow, and priestesses of Elune appear to ask who has disturbed it. They show what it once held: a gem through which they spoke with the goddess herself. To guard it Elune gave them the wildkin, fierce protectors of all her sacred places. Without her guidance the wildkin have grown feral and confused, yet wherever they are found they still guard something of importance.

parts.body: Erelas sends word straight to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus. Fandral is unmoved: the druids of the Cenarion Circle, he says, have long known that the wildkin are pets of Elune, chosen to guard the most sacred of places. It is not news, though he compliments the effort.
sources: quest 4902 reward text

title: Wild Guardians
body: Trull Failbane of Bloodvenom Post has heard that Winterspring, beyond Timbermaw northeast of Felwood, is laden with wildkin, beasts known to guard secrets of the night elves, and he means to learn what is hidden there. His knowledge of the owlbeasts themselves is said to be extensive. First the way must be opened. His hunters are sent against the ragged owlbeasts that range just south of the road and the raging owlbeasts of the valley's center, to clear them out and gain access to the land.

parts.body: With those beasts out of the way, the venture goes deeper. In the northern reaches of Winterspring the wildkin grow even more ferocious, and Trull sends his hunters after the moontouched owlbeasts there, to slay them and explore the ground they inhabit.

parts.body: Trull senses they are onto something. Runners back from Winterspring report a series of small caves in the south of the valley, ringed by wildkin. If the beasts guard anything of value, he believes it lies there, and the berserk owlbeasts of those caves seem to have gone mad from exposure to the very thing they protect.

parts.body: From the neck of a slain wildkin falls a necklace of blue feathers that glows brightly, slowly fading in and out. Trull knows a great deal about the owlbeasts but little of the magic they wield, so he sends the necklace on to one who can read it: Nara Wildmane in Thunder Bluff.

parts.body: Nara closes her eyes and senses only one source in the necklace's energy. The wildkin, misguided and confused as they are now, were not always so: the night elf goddess Elune created them to guard her most sacred places. It may seem a small thing, but she urges the bearer to look deeper. In time, she says, they will learn.
